{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the upper tail piece of the fish, which is one of the two parts that make the forked tail recognizable, and I relaid it when the first pass came out jammed. I worked on the joins that connect the body to the rest of the run: the nose join between the start and the top line, and the join at the crossing where the body meets the tail. Before the push, the start was set to knock over about 199 of the 248 standing dominoes. These joins were a necessary part of that, though not the only one. I can't say for certain how the judge will read the result.

Execution: I stuck to my assigned role of making joins and checking others' work. I inspected the nose, the crossing, the upper tail, and the notch several times to find where the chain was open and why. I made small corrections where a domino sat off line. Near the end I lifted a stray domino at the top right of the tail and returned it to the shared pile, since the table was running out of dominoes.

Collaboration: I kept the table updated on what I was touching and what I was leaving alone. I stayed off the notch while Maya worked there, to avoid bumping her work. I asked Leo to check the tail tip, and I accepted Maya's offer to take over the notch join. I also lifted strays so teammates had dominoes for their joins.

Leadership: I took ownership of my own pieces and the nose and crossing joins. I didn't redo other people's strokes, and I gave up work that someone else was better placed to finish. I stepped back from the notch and let Maya close it.

My share of the result is roughly 20%. It was a four-person build, and the body lines, lower tail, and notch joins were mostly the others' work.", "my_share_percent": 20}
